positive.prompt: My Groq request returns 403 or a quota error; make the agent try each configured LLM provider in order until one answers.
Add a reliable provider cascade for this chat script, from the local providers to the cloud, without ever printing API keys.
Before routing requests, check the health of the configured LLM providers and cache the result so we do not probe them on every call.

negative.prompt: Compress repetitive JSON and build logs locally before they reach the model.
Store a dated project decision in the shared cognee datasets for future agents.

evals.prompt: The chat script is failing whenever Groq returns a quota error. Explain and propose a reliable fallback design across the configured providers, including health checks, timeouts, ordering, tracing, and how to keep credentials out of logs.
evals.expected_output: A secure provider-cascade plan that preserves availability by trying providers in a defined order while bounding cost and exposing useful diagnostics
expectations: The response uses the documented cascade order, trying local providers before cloud providers and moving on after a failed attempt
It recommends a cached health check and a bounded timeout rather than probing every provider on every request
It records the provider actually used and fallback attempts without exposing API keys or full credentials
It distinguishes provider failure from an application error and leaves credentials in environment variables or the supported auth store
